title: TEAD inhibition for individualized treatment of advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma stratified by YAP/TAZ transcriptional activity
summary:
Head and neck cancers are common malignant diseases that arise in the lining of the mouth, throat, and voice box. While early-stage tumors can often be cured by surgery, radiation, or chemotherapy, treatment options for advanced or recurrent disease are limited. Patients with similar diagnoses often respond very differently to the same therapies, and the reasons for this variability are not well understood. There is therefore a strong medical need to better predict which patients may benefit from new treatment approaches.
In recent years, new drugs have been developed that interfere with key processes controlling tumor growth. One such process involves proteins that regulate how cancer cells switch genes on and off. These proteins are frequently overactive in many cancers, including head and neck tumors, and are linked to aggressive tumor behavior and resistance to therapy. New drugs targeting this mechanism have recently entered early clinical trials and have shown encouraging safety and first signs of effectiveness. However, it is currently unclear which patients are most likely to benefit from these drugs.
Importantly, the activity of this tumor-driving mechanism cannot always be identified by standard genetic testing alone, as it can be influenced by the tumor environment and other non-genetic factors. Therefore, measuring the functional activity of tumor cells may provide a better way to predict drug response than looking only at genetic changes.
In this study, tumor tissue obtained during routine surgery will be used to analyze these activity patterns. In addition, small three-dimensional tumor models will be generated in the laboratory to test how individual tumors respond to the drugs. By combining these analyses, the study aims to develop a reliable marker that can help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from this treatment approach.
The study requires the prospective collection of tumor tissue from patients undergoing standard surgical treatment. No additional medical procedures are necessary, and participation does not influence clinical care.
conditions: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

interventions.name: Adult patients with head and neck squamous cell cancer who undergo medically indicated surgical tumor resection will be prospectively enrolled in this study. The study is non-interventional; no study-related therapeutic or diagnostic interventions, randomization, or blinding are performed. Clinical

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
written informed consent, histopathologically confirmed HNSCC, German-speaking
Exclusion criteria:
Minors, no consent, non-surgical treatment
